correctness.rationale: For every \(k,m\ge1\), the proposed \(N_{k,m}(x)\) has nonnegative integer coefficients and zero constant term, so it defines the stated finite square-zero graded algebra. The coefficient of \(x^2\) on every off-diagonal entry is the positive integer \(m\), proving connectedness. The exact identity \(I+N=f_m I+p_-J\) splits over \(\mathbb Q\) into one scalar factor \(f_m+r p_-\) and \(k\) copies of \(f_m\). At \(x=1+t\), the latter has exact valuation \(m\), while the former has nonzero constant term \(r2^{m-1}\). Thus the Cartan local Smith exponents are \((0,m,\ldots,m)\), and inversion gives the claimed signed Euler–Smith profile. The argument is symbolic and uniform; no finite enumeration is used.

originality.rationale: The motivating full text makes connected realization modulo common shifts a residual problem and gives the two one-parameter boundary families \((-m,0)\) and \((-1,\ldots,-1,0)\), plus the isolated point \((-2,-2,0)\). The present direct formula realizes every pair \((k,m)\) simultaneously. Statement-level searches in the published-finding index and targeted literature searches found no statement implying the full two-parameter family. The construction is not a formal common shift of either boundary family: it changes the multiplicity of the negative elementary divisor while independently preserving its depth.
residual_risks: The motivating preprint is very recent, so an unindexed contemporaneous note could contain an equivalent elementary complete-graph construction.
The matrix identity \(fI+gJ\) is classical; originality is claimed only for its application to the stated connected signed Euler–Smith realization family, not for that linear-algebra identity.

value.rationale: The motivating paper itself singles out connected realization modulo common shifts as the nontrivial structured realization problem. Its inspected square-zero examples leave a natural two-parameter gap between arbitrary depth and arbitrary multiplicity. Filling the entire equal-depth grid with one explicit connected family is a structural realization lemma, not a routine numerical extension: it shows that depth and multiplicity of a negative elementary divisor can be prescribed independently inside connected radical-square-zero algebras.
